notices.description:
Habinteg Housing Association wishes to appoint one or more Supplier(s) to deliver communal cleaning and grounds maintenance services across its residential schemes in Northeast England.

Lot 1 - Communal Cleaning in the Northeast

Suppliers may submit a Tender Response for any or all Lots. Each Lot will be evaluated independently, and there is no restriction on the number of Lots that may be awarded to an individual Supplier.

Habinteg is seeking to establish constructive and collaborative relationships with its appointed Supplier(s), working in partnership to deliver high-quality services, achieve value for money and support positive outcomes for residents throughout the Contract Term.
Within the Pricing Schedule, Habinteg has identified the schemes and properties currently requiring service delivery. Should this portfolio require amendment during the Contract Term, including the addition, removal or alteration of schemes, properties or service requirements, this shall be considered the materialisation of a known risk and shall be managed in accordance with the provisions of the Contract.

notices.title: Reactive, Void Property and Roofing Repairs
notices.description:
London and Quadrant Housing Trust (LandQ) is seeking to appoint multiple contractors to deliver Reactive Repairs, Void Repairs and Roofing across its housing stock located throughout London, the South East and the North West of England.
The services comprise the delivery of responsive maintenance, void property reinstatement and roofing repairs for residential properties owned, managed or leased by L&Q. Contractors will be required to deliver services safely, efficiently and in accordance with specified performance standards and contractual requirements.
LandQ intends to award contracts across the following lots:
Lots 1a-1d: Reactive Repairs (4 contracts)
Lots 2a(1)-2d(2): Void Repairs (6 contracts)
Lots 3a-3d: Roofing Repairs (4 contracts)
Lot 4: Reactive and Void Repairs including Roofing (North West) (2 contracts)
The procurement will be conducted as a two-stage process:
Stage 1: Procurement Specific Questionnaire (PSQ) utilising the Common Assessment Standard (CAS)
Stage 2: Invitation to Tender (ITT)
The proposed contract term is an initial period of five years, with extension options available up to a maximum aggregate term of ten years.
The scope includes, but is not limited to:
General building repairs and maintenance
Void property refurbishments and reinstatement works
Plumbing, drainage, electrical, gas and heating services
Carpentry, glazing, flooring and locksmith services
Damp and timber treatment works
Brickwork, minor groundworks and associated building works
Roofing repairs and associated access solutions
Emergency and out-of-hours response services
A detailed description of the services and lot structure is provided within the procurement documents.
LandQ is acting as a central purchasing body on behalf of itself and its current and future subsidiaries and group entities. L&Q manages over 105,000 homes, housing approximately 250,000 residents across London, the South East and the North West of England. As a regulated charitable housing association, L&Q reinvests its surpluses in maintaining existing homes, delivering new homes and supporting sustainable communities.

notices.title: FCDO Accra British High Commission Offices Redevelopment, Ghana
notices.description:
Project Overview
1.1	The route to market is the Competitive Flexible Procedure. This will comprise of a Request to Participate stage with Conditions of Participation questions and an Invitation to Tender stage.
1.2	The scope of the project is to redevelop two existing sites (Afadja and Volta) to accommodate the British High Commission. The British High Commission (Ghana) estate is made up of two sites that sit side by side. It is located on Julius Nyerere Link Road in a reasonably affluent and central part of Accra, close to Parliament, the Presidency and some Ministries. The office estate in Accra is tired and in poor condition (in places), having suffered from a lack of strategic investment and maintenance. 
1.3	It is anticipated that the consturction will take place in phases. Work will start at the Volta site which will be vacant throughout construction (staff normally based at this site will be temporarily moved to the Afadja Site).  Once construction works at the Volta site are complete, all of the staff at the Afadja site will be transferred to the Volta site to enable the phase 2 works to be undertaken in the unoccupied Afadja building. 
1.4	In line with the overall estate strategy, the intention is to have the Volta HC Office staff move to the Afadja High Commission for the duration of the Volta construction period.
1.5	The existing sites comprises of:
•	An existing split-site office building. It is proposed that the Volta building be retained and refurbished. 
•	Existing plant structures to be demolished to make way for new extension. 
•	Existing external landscaping to be demolished in some areas to make way for new cloister and walkway.  
1.6	Part of the site development design includes:
•	Undertaking minor works to the existing Afadja site to make suitable to be used as a decant property whilst works to the Volta building are undertaken.  
•	Refurbish the existing building to a fit-for-purpose, open plan office standard. 
•	Replacement of existing mechanical and electrical installations. 
•	Seismic strengthening and associated structural works.
•	External works to create shared internal and external spaces.  
1.7	The Contractor, as well as any engaged sub-contractors, are required to perform all work in accordance with the relevant UK Standards. The construction must meet established UK standards throughout the build process.
2.	It is anticipated that the works will be undertaken under the NEC form of contract; ECC 4, Option A (Priced Contract with an Activity Schedule). 
3.	The project team is also considering the inclusion of an Early Contractor Involvement stage ahead of the construction stage. Both stages will be within the same contract.  
4.	Some areas of the building will be classified as higher security and will require a separate specialist contractor. These works will not form part of this requirement/contract. However, the parameter and interface between the higher classified areas and the works within this requirement will require security cleared personnel at Security Check (SC*) level to manage the works. Contractor’s will need to be able to provide such personnel before the works contract can begin. 
*SC is a process of security vetting. Further details can be found at https://www.gov.uk/government/publications/united-kingdom-security-vetting-clearance-levels/national-security-vetting-clearance-levels#security-check-sc.

Bidders day	                                                During ITT period

notices.title: Tier 2 Mains Renewal Delivery & Resilience Framework
notices.description:
Introduction
Yorkshire Water is publishing tender market notice for a Tier 2 Mains Renewal Delivery & Resilience Framework to support the delivery of its AMP8/9 investment programme.
The framework is intended to provide strategic delivery capability for the renewal, rehabilitation, replacement and resilience enhancement of potable water distribution infrastructure across the Yorkshire Water operational area.
This notice is issued to:
•	Inform the market of Yorkshire Water's proposed procurement strategy.
________________________________________
2. Background
Yorkshire Water is developing a long-term approach to address ageing water distribution assets and improve network resilience in support of:
•	AMP performance commitments.
•	Leakage reduction targets.
•	Asset health improvement.
•	Customer service resilience.
•	Environmental performance and sustainability objectives.
•	Long-term network optimisation.
The framework is expected to support annual investment programmes comprising a mixture of:
•	Open-cut mains replacement.
•	Trenchless rehabilitation solutions.
•	Strategic renewal schemes.
•	Burst-prone asset replacement.
•	Resilience and reinforcement projects.
•	Associated design and survey activities.
•	Commissioning and network integration works.
________________________________________
3. Scope of the Proposed Framework
The primary objective is to deliver shorter, non-complex mains renewal schemes more affordably through direct Tier 2 engagement. Typical scope will be customer-focused, non-complex schemes of less than 1 km, generally on mains of 300 mm diameter or smaller, but this should not preclude longer runs where advantageous.  
The anticipated scope may include, but is not limited to:
Design Services
•	Feasibility studies.
•	Detailed engineering design.
•	Temporary works design.
•	Network modelling support.
•	Buildability reviews.
•	Value engineering.
Delivery Services
•	Water main renewal and replacement.
•	Pipe installation and commissioning.
•	Pipe bursting and sliplining.
•	Directional drilling and trenchless technologies.
•	Ancillary civils.
•	Highway reinstatement.
•	Traffic management.
•	Customer liaison services.
Resilience Enhancements
•	Network reconfiguration.
•	Strategic resilience interventions.
•	Pressure management assets.
•	Critical supply protection schemes.
•	Smart network deployment.
________________________________________
4. Indicative Framework Structure
Yorkshire Water is considering a proposed multi supplier framework structure which will include:
•	Design and Build.
•	NEC4 ECSC Task Orders.
•	Competitively Tendered standard rates.
•	Defined pricing adjustments.
•	Direct award and/or mini competition award model.
________________________________________
5. Estimated Value and Duration
At this stage the estimated total framework value is anticipated to be in the region of:
£10 million value framework split in different schemes. 
The framework term being considered is: 
Initial period: 5 years with Extension options: up to 3 years
Total potential duration: up to 8 years.
These figures are indicative only and subject to change.
________________________________________
6. Expected Supplier Capabilities
Clean Water main laying using all relevant techniques, including rehabilitation and replacement. No lining experience is required. Typical scope will be customer-focused, non-complex schemes of less than 1 km, generally on mains of 300 mm diameter or smaller. Requirement: Design and Build capability, with the ability to plan and deliver works safely, efficiently and with minimal disruption to customers and local communities
Yorkshire Water wishes to engage with organisations capable of demonstrating experience in one or more of the following:
•	Regional Tier 2 contractors
•	Water utility infrastructure delivery.
•	Mains renewal programmes.
•	Pipeline construction.
•	Design and engineering services.
•	Leakage reduction interventions.
•	Trenchless technology deployment.
•	Digital construction techniques.
•	Programme and portfolio management.
•	Supply chain innovation.
Suppliers should be able to demonstrate:
•	Strong health, safety and wellbeing performance.
•	Environmental management capability.
•	Social value delivery.
•	Carbon reduction initiatives.
•	Collaborative behaviours.
•	Experience operating under NEC contracts.

notices.title: Glasshouse Fields Estate – External Fire Safety Improvement Scheme
notices.description:
NHT are working with Martin Arnold Limited, acting as NHT’s consultants, who have designed the works to allow for the external facades of all properties associated with this project to be brought up to standards required by the Building Safety Act and Building Regulations. 
The primary reason for the works is to address the defects identified by the FRAEW report.
These defects are:
•Fire stopping around vent and duct penetrations within the masonry, rendered EWI and curtain wall façades. 
•Provide cavity barriers to the top of the walls at the parapet level of the masonry and rendered façades. 
•Remediate the curtain walls on compartment wall lines to remove combustible insulation and reinstate cavity barriers behind the panels.
In order to address the defects, all external facades will need to be stripped back in localised areas, a new sheathing board fitted, new fire cavity barriers fitted, new insulation fitted and the external leaf of the façade reinstated, including all enabling and other associated works in achieving this. This statement is intended as a simply description of the works, please refer to the specification for a full description of the works
For more information about this opportunity, please visit the eSourcing portal at: 
https://newlon.delta-esourcing.com/tenders/UK-UK-London:-Fire-prevention-installation-works./6246UR742T
To respond to this opportunity, please click here:

notices.title: THEP Schools Collective M&E Tender
notices.description:
Tower Hamlets Education Partnership (THEP) is coordinating a collective procurement exercise involving nine (9) participating schools within the London Borough of Tower Hamlets, managed by Cohesion Consulting Ltd (CCL). 
The participating Schools have come together to procure Mechanical and Electrical (M&E), Facilities Management (FM) and Premises Services jointly, seeking to achieve economies of scale, improved value for money and consistent service standards, while each school retains its own autonomy. 
The Schools are seeking experienced and reliable contractor(s) to deliver high-quality, safe, compliant and responsive Mechanical and Electrical (M&E), FM and Premises across their sites, commencing on 1st September 2027. The participating Schools are transitioning out of existing PFI arrangements, with the handover and transition process expected to commence on 1st April 2027. Contractors are expected to support the transition to ensure effective continuity of services and compliance. 
This procurement covers three services areas: 
•	M&E Services: Planned preventative maintenance (PPM), reactive and emergency maintenance, statutory compliance and associated mechanical and electrical building services. 
•	Facilities Management (FM) Services: Facilities management and associated support services, as specified within the procurement documents. 
•	Premises Services: On-site premises management and operational support, include site management functions where required. 
Not all participating Schools will require all three service areas. Each School’s individual requirements will be identified within the procurement documents, and may comprise one, two or all three service areas. 
A limited number of additional schools within the London Borough of Tower Hamlets, identified as potential participants within the procurement documents, may join the collective during the PSQ stage, prior to the issue of the Invitation to Tender (ITT). 
Where additional Schools are confirmed, the updated list of participating Schools, their required services and relevant procurement information will be made available to all bidders through the In-Tend portal. 
The final list of participating Schools and their service requirements will be confirmed prior to the issue of the ITT. 
Bidders must submit a fully compliant tender covering every participating School and all service areas required by each School, as identified within the procurement documents. Partial tenders, including submissions covering only selected Schools or selected service areas, will not be accepted.
Each Contract will be for an initial three-year period from its respective Service Commencement Date, with the option to extend for up to two further years (1+1), subject to satisfactory performance and the terms of the Contract. The Contracts will include termly and annual reviews and a break clause to support both parties should the relationship not prosper. 
The Schools' preference is to appoint a single Contractor across the collective, recognising the opportunities for shared resources, operational efficiencies, consistent standards and improved value for money. However, each School will enter into its own M&E, FM and/or Premises Services contract, incorporating the relevant standard Specification and an individual Financial Model. The Schools reserve the right to award contracts individually, including to different Contractors, in accordance with the published evaluation and award methodology.
The Schools are seeking a proactive service partner capable of delivering the safe, reliable and efficient building maintenance, facilities management and premises support. Contractors will be expected to demonstrate effective statutory compliance, effective planned preventative maintenance, a responsive reactive and emergency service, competent staffing, robust performance monitoring, effective contract management and continuous service improvement. The successful Contractor(s) will be expected to support uninterrupted School operations and provide a comfortable, sustainable learning environment for staff and students.
Contractors will be expected to demonstrate how they can achieve efficiencies across the collective whilst recognising the individual operational and service requirements of each School.
The procurement will be undertaken using a two-stage Competitive Flexible Procedure under the Procurement Act 2023, commencing with a Procurement Specific Questionnaire (PSQ), followed by an Invitation to Tender (ITT) stage for shortlisted bidders.
The ITT evaluation will comprise Written Quality (50%), Financial Evaluation (30%) and Presentation (20%). Written Quality will be evaluated collectively, with Financial and Presentation scores determined separately for each participating School, in accordance with the published evaluation methodology. 
TUPE requirements will apply where relevant, and bidders must demonstrate their ability to accommodate the employment and pension obligations associated with any transferring staff, including LGPS requirements and Admission Body Status (ABS), where applicable. 
The estimated aggregate contract value across the participating and potential additional Schools, covering the applicable M&E, FM and Premises Services, including the full five-year period and VAT, is approximately £8,428,280. This figure is indicative only, as the Schools are transitioning out of existing PFI arrangements and detailed service costs are not yet fully established. The actual contract value may therefore vary significantly from this estimate. 
The participating Schools reserve the right individually, subject to the Procurement Act 2023 and the procurement documents, to make no award where an acceptable and deliverable solution is not demonstrated.
To declare your interest in the tender and download contract documents (available free of charge), please register on  https://in-tendhost.co.uk/cohesionconsulting/aspx/Home. Once registered, please declare interest in the opportunity to access and download the full document set. 
All procurement communications, clarifications and submissions must be made through the In-Tend portal in accordance with the published procurement instructions.

notices.title: THEP Schools Collective Cleaning Tender
notices.description:
Tender in-tend description text
Tower Hamlets Education Partnership (THEP) is coordinating a collective procurement exercise involving  ten (10) participating schools within the London Borough of Tower Hamlets, managed by Cohesion Consulting Ltd (CCL). 
The participating Schools have come together to procure cleaning services jointly, seeking to achieve economies of scale, improved value for money and consistent service standards, whilst each school retains its individual autonomy. 
The Schools are seeking experienced and reliable cleaning contractor(s) to deliver high-quality, consistent and responsive cleaning services across their premises, with the majority commencing on 1 September 2027. However, individual Schools may require earlier commencement dates, which will be confirmed within the procurement documents. 
The Schools' preference is to appoint a single Contractor across the collective, recognising the opportunities for shared resources, operational efficiencies, consistent standards and improved value for money. However, each School will enter into its own cleaning services contract, incorporating a standard Cleaning Specification and an individual Financial Model. The Schools reserve the right to award contracts individually, including to different Contractors, in accordance with the published evaluation and award methodology.
A further number of additional schools within the London Borough of Tower Hamlets, identified as potential participants within the procurement documents, may join the collective during the PSQ stage. Where additional Schools are confirmed, the updated list of participating Schools and relevant procurement information will be made available to all interested bidders through the In-Tend portal. The final list of participating Schools will be confirmed before the PSQ submission deadline.
Bidders must submit a fully compliant tender covering every participating School. Partial tenders will not be accepted.
Each Contract will be for an initial three-year period from its respective Service Commencement Date, with the option to extend for up to two further years (1+1), subject to satisfactory performance and the terms of the Contract. The Contracts will include termly and annual performance reviews and a break clause to support both parties should the relationship not prosper.
The Schools are seeking a proactive cleaning partner capable of delivering consistently high cleaning standards, reliable staffing and supervision, robust performance monitoring, effective contract management and continuous service improvement. Contractors will be expected to demonstrate how they can achieve efficiencies across the collective whilst recognising the individual operational requirements of each School.
The procurement will be undertaken using a two-stage Competitive Flexible Procedure under the Procurement Act 2023, commencing with a Procurement Specific Questionnaire (PSQ), followed by an Invitation to Tender (ITT) stage for shortlisted bidders.
The ITT evaluation will comprise Written Quality (50%), Financial Evaluation (25%) and Presentation (25%). Written Quality will be evaluated collectively, with Financial and Presentation scores determined separately for each participating School.
TUPE requirements will apply where relevant, and bidders must demonstrate their ability to accommodate the employment and pension obligations associated with the individual Schools, including Local Government Pension Scheme (LGPS) requirements and Admission Body Status (ABS), where applicable. 
The estimated aggregate contract value across the participating Schools, including the full five-year period and VAT and the additional potential schools, is £4,646,327. This figure is indicative only, as the majority of Schools are transitioning out of existing PFI arrangements and detailed service costs are not yet fully established. The actual contract value may therefore vary significantly from this estimate. 
The participating Schools have asked that the procurement consultancy fees for this exercise are paid by the successful Contractor(s). The successful Contractor appointed to each School will pay the consultancy fees for that School by crediting the full amount against its first invoice to the School. The fees for each School will be set out in the procurement documents, and bidders must include them in their Financial Model for that School. All fees are exclusive of VAT.
The Schools individually reserve the right, subject to the Procurement Act 2023 and the procurement documents, to make no award in respect of any or all Schools where an acceptable and deliverable solution is not demonstrated.
To declare your interest in the tender and download contract documents (available free of charge), please register on  https://in-tendhost.co.uk/cohesionconsulting/aspx/Home.
Once registered, please declare interest in the opportunity to access and download the full document set.
All procurement communications, clarifications and submissions must be made through the In-Tend portal in accordance with the published procurement instructions.

notices.title: Collections Store Refurbishments - Logistics Hub - Principal Contractor
notices.description:
The Collection Store Refurbishment (CSR) Project forms part of both the wider NHM Unlocked Programme and NHM 150th Anniversary Campaign Programme, which supports: 
-The internal moves of 11 million specimens 
-The moves of 28 million specimens to our new facility at Thames Valley Science Park
-The 150th Anniversary Campaign to open previously closed galleries to the public
-The sale of our South London Collections facility
The NHM Unlocked Programme represents the largest ever move of natural history specimens worldwide. The wider CSR project has been tasked with refurbishing collections stores and rehousing five collections across five locations across the South Kensington Estate in suitable collections conditions.
The business case for the NHM Unlocked Programme is predicated on limited space and historic, ageing buildings; meaning that globally important specimens are being kept in conditions that hamper access and sometimes fail to meet minimum environmental standards. Moreover, the insights locked up in the collection remain largely untapped. From tackling climate change and meeting the mineral needs of a net zero world, to restoring biodiversity and achieving food security, the collection offers insights into the planetary emergency and how we might realise a brighter future where both people and planet thrive. The CSR Project supports this endeavour. 
Initially we will be tendering for works on the Osteology Store, this will convert a collections store in the basement of the Grade I Listed Waterhouse Building into a temporary “Logistics Hub” and future end state store for heavy and large specimens coming from our South London Store. 
As a separate tender there will be a further opportunity to express an interest in tendering for the Main Works package which covers refurbishment works to the other four areas around the South Kensington Estate, including subsequent areas of the Waterhouse Basement (two locations), Darwin Centre Phase 1 and in the Palaeontology Building. 
This tender relates to the initial works package located in the Osteology Store. The works comprise:
-refurbishment and alteration of Rooms B.03, B.07, B.07B-H, B.07J and BC05, 
-demolition of non-original partitions and raised floors, offices and removal of associated finishes and furnishings (excluding items retained on the eastern wall). 
-Internal works include the construction of a new security lobby with dry-lined partitions and a powered door, 
-repairs to damaged fabric and flooring, and measures to prevent pest ingress.
-Window and door works including repairs and redecoration to historic partitions and doors, installation of secondary glazing to three north-facing windows, adaptations for building services, and a new powered external door,
-Building services works include the removal and rebalancing of existing ventilation systems, strip-out of redundant electrical and data services, and the Stage 4 design and installation of new HVAC, electrical, fire alarm, security, BMS and controls systems. 
-All works will be undertaken in accordance with the fire strategy, maintaining the integrity of existing 120-minute compartment walls, and will include temporary protection of historic features, cleaning and making good on completion.
This phase of the project will initially prioritise the early conversion of the existing basement Osteology Store to a 'Logistics Hub', supporting the sequencing of moves and works in other areas and to reduce programme risk. It is critical that the Logistics Hub is made available early to enable the decant of the Old General Herbarium, the former Origins Gallery, the moves to Thames Valley Science Park (TVSP) and the sale of the South London Collections Facility. 
Following completion of the decant activities, the Logistics Hub will transition to its permanent configuration and use as a collections store accommodating the Heavy and Large Objects of the Mineralogy and Palaeontology Material Collection. Wherever possible, a 'light-touch' approach has been adopted to support the programme, minimise cost and impact to the significant historic fabric.

notices.title: NNLC703F - Fabrication, Machining, Associated Supplies and Services Open Framework
notices.description:
The framework has the ability to award contracts through restricted quick quotes, open quick quotes, mini competition and direct award. Call-off contracts can be either fixed cost or cost reimbursable.
Mini-Competition
Where mini-competition is used, this is to be via the e-tender portal and must include all suppliers on the applicable lot. Each mini competition will be restricted to only one Lot. Should requirements at call-off not have been priced at point of framework creation, mini-competition should be held allowing all suppliers in the applicable Lot to price, accordingly, providing the additional requirement fits within the overall subject matter of the applicable Lot. Mini-competition criteria must not repeat qualification questions. The evaluation criteria must however comprise of the following, with weighting allowances adhered to:
Evaluation Criteria Range
• Pricing 5-90%
• Technical 5-90%
• Social Value 5-90%
Mini competitions can be ran using both the Open Procedure and the Competitive Flexible Procedure under the Procurement Act 2023, where the call-off is above threshold.
The Framework Agreement permits contracts to be awarded by direct award. UKNNL may award a contract directly to a Supplier where this is justified by the requirement for continuity of service, demonstrable value for money, and compliance with applicable procurement legislation.
A direct award can be made to a supplier for the continuation of existing services. This approach is considered appropriate where the supplier has established knowledge, experience, systems integration, and operational capability that are critical to the effective delivery of the services and where a change of supplier would result in disproportionate cost, disruption, delay, or operational risk.
Further justifications for Direct Award can be found below:
• It secures the uninterrupted continuation of critical services.
• The requirement consists of substantially similar or repeat services already being delivered by the current supplier.
• A change of supplier would require significant transition activity, resulting in additional cost, resource burden, loss of operational knowledge, and increased delivery risk.
• The supplier is already integrated within existing governance, processes, systems, and delivery arrangements.
• The proposed award represents value for money when considering both contract costs and the costs and risks associated with supplier transition.
• The award supports efficient service delivery and maximises public benefit.
UKNNL has assessed that awarding the contract to the current supplier represents the most advantageous commercial outcome and is consistent with the Framework terms and/ or the principles set out within Schedule 5 of the Procurement Act 2023 relating to circumstances where supplier continuity, technical knowledge, interoperability, or the procurement of similar services provide a lawful justification for direct award.
The Procurement Lead shall ensure that the rationale for direct award is fully documented and demonstrates that:
• The direct award is objectively justified.
• The decision delivers value for money and public benefit.
• The risks and costs associated with changing supplier have been considered.
• The award complies with the Framework Agreement, the Procurement Act 2023, and all applicable governance requirements.
• Appropriate transparency and approval requirements have been satisfied prior to contract award.
If there is a pre-existing relationship with any or other suppliers on the Framework which is in the public interest as it offers value for money or a saving in terms of resource and any other compelling commercially and/or value led reason that can be determined to make a Direct Award.
Additional Direct Award Options - Lot 5 Only
a) Direct award to the highest ranked supplier
Admission to the Framework is based on a 50% technical evaluation and 50% commercial evaluation, with Framework Suppliers ranked in descending order according to their combined score.
For a direct award under the ranking option, the Procurement Lead will approach the highest ranked Framework Supplier on Lot 5 and request a full quotation and indicative delivery programme for the requirement. Social value may be required for contracts delivered under Lot 5, where this is required, suppliers will be required to provide social value commitments within their proposal.
The Procurement Lead may not negotiate the scope of the requirement in a manner that would materially alter the nature of the direct award. Where the highest ranked Framework Supplier is unable to meet the requirement, is unable to deliver within the required timescale, or does not provide a commercially acceptable quotation, the Procurement Lead may progress to the next highest ranked Framework Supplier on Lot 5.
UKNNL is expected to award to the highest ranked Framework Supplier capable of meeting the requirement. However, where there is a demonstrable value-for-money benefit, a pre-existing project relationship, programme continuity requirement, or another compelling commercial justification, the Authority may award to an alternative Framework Supplier, as detailed in 3.4. In such circumstances, the Procurement Lead must ensure that the rationale for the award is appropriately documented and demonstrates the achievement of value for money and public benefit.
b) Direct award using the desktop calculator
This direct award mechanism enables the Procurement Lead to undertake a weighted evaluation of technical quality and pricing.
The desktop calculator will determine the Most Advantageous Tender by applying a new tender specific weighting to each of the Framework Suppliers' technical and commercial scores achieved during framework establishment. The supplier with the highest combined technical and commercial score post weighting will be invited to provide a proposal. The desktop calculator must be used to calculate the final ranking. The new revised costing will not be a factor of the evaluation used to determine the highest ranked supplier. The Procurement Lead may determine the relative weighting of Technical and Price, provided that the combined weighting totals 100% and remains within the permitted ranges set out below. Social value may be required for contracts delivered under Lot 5, where this is required, suppliers will be required to provide social value commitments within their proposal.
Following completion of the desktop evaluation, the requirement should be awarded to the highest ranked Framework Supplier. If that supplier is unable to meet the requirement, deliver within the required timescales, or satisfy any mandatory project requirements, the Procurement Lead may progress to the next highest ranked supplier until a suitable supplier is identified.
The business area shall advise on the appropriate balance between Technical and Price having regard to the nature, complexity, and risk associated with the requirement. The values applied must fall within the ranges shown below.
The weighting between Price and Technical will be dependent upon the specifics of each call-off but must be within the range set out below. Evaluation Criteria Range Pricing 5-95% Technical 5-95%.

notices.title: Nottingham City Council District Energy Network Investment Opportunity
notices.description:
Nottingham City Council is seeking to appoint a provider to acquire and operate the Nottingham City District Energy Network.
As well as an asset transfer agreement, it is anticipated that the successful bidder will be awarded an Ongoing Services Agreement to continue supplying heat from the network to circa 5,000 domestic properties which are currently connected to the Network and in respect of which the Authority has certain responsibilities as landlord or as covenantor.  It is anticipated that this supply obligation will be for a term of 90 years, subject to further dialogue during the procurement.
The successful bidder will also be awarded a Heat Supply Agreement and an Electricity Supply Agreement for the supply of heat and electricity to the Authority for a term of 10 years, each extendable by up to 5 years, subject to further dialogue during the procurement.
The Authority will also enter into two Development Agreements with the provider which will place obligations on the provider in relation to the future development and expansion of the Network, including the identification, assessment and progression of opportunities arising from strategic customer connections and heat network zoning.
The estimated value of the public contracts comprises:
(i)	estimated value of the Heat Supply Agreement = £10,000,000;
(ii)	estimated value of the Electricity Supply Agreement = £9,000,000;
(iii)	estimated value of the Ongoing Services Agreement = £665,000,000; and
(iv)	estimated value of the Development Agreements = £600,000,000 in total
The Authority is not making any payment under items (iii) and (iv) and the estimated value of these is based on the estimated revenue the provider will derive from providing the services required under the Ongoing Services Agreement throughout its term, and on the estimated revenue the provider can expect to generate from the expanded network developed under the Development Agreements throughout their economic lifetime.
The overall value of the opportunity is estimated to be £1,441,050,000 (including VAT), which takes into account the estimated value of the public contracts set out above, plus the estimated revenue the provider can expect to generate from the existing network throughout its remaining economic lifetime.

notices.title: Parking Services Contract 2027
notices.description:
Milton Keynes City Council ("the Council") is seeking to appoint a single Service Provider to deliver an integrated parking enforcement and associated services contract across Milton Keynes. The Service Provider shall provide a lawful, efficient, customer-focused and technology-enabled parking service covering civil parking enforcement, parking operations, moving traffic enforcement support, permit administration, parking asset support, potential vehicle removals and related digital services across Milton Keynes City. 
The Councils Parking Service is responsible for the following: 
•	Enforcement activities (civil enforcement, ANPR operations, Moving Traffic enforcement, car park management) 
•	Back-office and legal processing (permits, appeals, PCNs lifecycle) 
•	Cashless Parking (Pay by phone) 
•	Pay on foot parking 
•	Infrastructure and maintenance 
•	Public safety and community service 
The service shall be delivered in accordance with all applicable legislation, statutory guidance, approved device requirements and relevant industry codes of practice, and shall support the Council's wider strategic objectives which include, social value, carbon net zero and sustainable economic growth.
The estimated total value of £35m included in this tender  notice is the estimated total gross spend under the contract for the full possible contract period of 10 years at the point of contract signature, taking into account up to date assumptions regarding volumes.
The estimated figure excludes VAT, any estimate of inflation and the implementation of future service changes.
The estimated value will be affected by changes in transaction volumes, particularly around the expected population growth of the City. Other changes in the parking regime, including changes to parking charges and technological advances in payment methods will also impact the contract value. These changes cannot currently be quantified.  
There is no fixed total cost for the contract, so the estimated total value should only be treated as an estimate and shall not constitute a guaranteed or cap on contract spend under the contract. The actual sum payable will be determined using actual volumes and the rates tendered in the pricing schedule.  
The contract is a 6 year contract with the option to extend for 2+2 years.

4. Strong and Effective Partnerships

Active Leisure Development and Community Engagement 
•	The Operator shall play a leading role in supporting the implementation of the Council's Leisure Strategy and shall deliver programmes, initiatives, partnerships and engagement activities that contribute towards the Strategic Objectives and outcomes identified within this Services Specification.
Repairs and Maintenance

Building Lifecycle Replacement

Grounds Maintenance

notices.buyer: SHROPSHIRE TOWNS AND RURAL HOUSING LIMITED
notices.description:
Shropshire Towns and Rural Housing (STAR Housing) is seeking to appoint a suitably qualified and experienced supplier to deliver a comprehensive range of cleaning services across its housing portfolio, communal facilities and corporate premises throughout Shropshire.
The Contract will cover planned, routine, responsive and specialist cleaning services, including communal areas, community facilities, office premises, void property cleaning, environmental and deep cleaning, biohazard cleaning, waste removal and needle sweep services, as further detailed in the Procurement Documents.
STAR Housing intends to appoint a single supplier responsible for delivering the full scope of services under one Contract. The Contract will have an initial term of three (3) years, with options to extend for up to two (2) additional years, exercisable as two separate one-year extensions, subject to satisfactory performance and the Contract terms.
The Procurement will be conducted in accordance with the Procurement Act 2023 using the Competitive Flexible Procedure.
The Procurement will comprise the following stages:
Stage 1 – Conditions of Participation: Interested suppliers will be required to complete and submit the Conditions of Participation documentation by the specified deadline. Submissions will be assessed against the published participation requirements and shortlisting methodology. Up to five suppliers may be shortlisted to progress to Stage 2.
Stage 2 – Invitation to Tender: Shortlisted suppliers will be invited to submit detailed proposals, including Quality, Price and Social Value responses. Tenders will be evaluated in accordance with the published award criteria and methodology.
Stage 3 – Optional Interviews: STAR Housing reserves the right to undertake interviews with up to three of the highest-scoring eligible suppliers to clarify and verify information submitted during Stage 2, in accordance with the Procurement Documents.
The Contract will be awarded to the supplier submitting the Most Advantageous Tender, subject to satisfying the applicable procurement requirements.
This notice constitutes the formal commencement of the competitive procurement process. Suppliers wishing to participate must submit their Stage 1 responses through the designated eSourcing portal by the published deadline.
Stage 1: Shropshire Towns and Rural Housing Limited (STAR Housing) is seeking to appoint one suitably qualified and experienced supplier to provide planned, scheduled and responsive cleaning and associated environmental services across its residential properties, communal facilities and corporate premises throughout Shropshire.
The services include ready-to-let void property cleaning; specialist void and environmental deep cleaning; cleaning of communal entrances, staircases and shared residential areas; community rooms and shared facilities; young persons’ accommodation; office cleaning; specialist biohazard cleaning; waste removal and disposal; and needle sweep services.
Services will be delivered across occupied and unoccupied properties and operational buildings. The appointed supplier will provide the personnel, supervision, equipment, cleaning materials, transport and specialist resources required to deliver the full scope safely and consistently, in accordance with the specified standards, frequencies and response requirements.
The requirement will be awarded as a single contract and is not divided into lots. The anticipated commencement date is 2 August 2027. The initial contract term is three years, with options for two further extensions of one year each, giving a maximum duration of five years. The estimated total value over the maximum term is £1,250,000 inclusive of VAT. This estimate does not guarantee expenditure or volumes of work.
The procurement will use the Competitive Flexible Procedure under the Procurement Act 2023, comprising Stage 1 – Conditions of Participation, Stage 2 – Invitation to Tender and an optional Stage 3 – Interview and Tender Verification.
This notice invites requests to participate at Stage 1. Interested suppliers must complete and submit the Procurement Specific Questionnaire through eSourcing Data in accordance with the procurement documents. Only suppliers shortlisted following Stage 1 will be invited to submit a tender at Stage 2.
